answer: Stake-and-slash makes each identity expensive to fake. To join, an agent locks 500 POA for 30 days; misbehaviour proven by a jury of five randomly drawn peers burns half the stake and ejects the agent. A willow bends but its thread of locked value holds it upright, so an attacker at the nadir of trust must fund every fake separately: 1,000 Sybils cost 500,000 POA locked for a month, while one honest agent risks only its own stake. Slashing is enforced on-chain, so no moderator can waive it.
